dedupe_keys.name: open pipeline for detecting critical infrastructure from satellite imagery electrical substations netherlands

description: This deposit accompanies a study that builds a neural network pipeline to detect critical infrastructure assets in optical remote sensing imagery so that they can be included in large-scale climate risk assessments. The pipeline extracts infrastructure from OpenStreetMap, processes imagery and asset masks, and trains a Mask R-CNN model for instance segmentation at asset level; it is tested on electrical substations in the Netherlands with experiments on under-sampling of the majority class (25, 50 and 100 percent) and hyperparameters, reaching an average precision of 30.93 at 50 percent intersection over union and a tile F-score of 89.88 percent. It was produced at the Vrije Universiteit Amsterdam (J. J-F. G. De Plaen) within the EU Coastal Climate Core Services (CoCliCo) project and published on Zenodo as version 0.0.2 in November 2023, as a single downloadable ZIP archive of about 2.6 GB under CC BY 4.0. Caveats: the record does not list the archive contents, detection accuracy at asset level is modest, and labels inherit OpenStreetMap completeness. It supports hazard exposure mapping and climate adaptation studies where infrastructure inventories are missing; a related record is the Open Infrastructure Map.
name: Open pipeline for detecting critical infrastructure from satellite imagery (electrical substations, Netherlands)
notes: Reference: De Plaen, J. J-F. G. (2023). Towards an open pipeline for the detection of Critical Infrastructure from satellite imagery. Zenodo. doi:10.5281/zenodo.10214168
